title: Problems with UTF-8 encoded queries on Windows (with cross platform db)
description:
# The Problem

I am a little perplexed by a behavior I am experiencing with a SQLite database generate on Linux system when consumed on Windows (Mac users report that everything works fine) ... 

Assume you **create the following DB on a Linux system** (aka UTF-8 native):

```r
# packages
library(RSQLite)

# connect
con <- dbConnect(SQLite(), "test_encoding.db")

# make table
dbWriteTable(
  con, 
  "test_table", 
  data.frame(col_one = "άνγκελα_μέρκελ")
)

# read whole table
dbGetQuery(con, "select * from test_table")$col_one
## [1] "άνγκελα_μέρκελ"

# query for specific line
dbGetQuery(con, "select * from test_table where col_one = 'άνγκελα_μέρκελ'")$col_one
## [1] "άνγκελα_μέρκελ"

# close connection
dbDisconnect(con)
```

Now **when consuming on a Windows system** the data is there and **BUT the query does not work**:


```r
# packages
library(RSQLite)

# get database
download.file(
  "http://petermeissner.de/downloads/test_encoding.db",
  "test_encoding.db",
  mode = "wb"
)

# connect
con <- dbConnect(SQLite(), "test_encoding.db")

# read whole table
dbGetQuery(con, "select * from test_table")$col_one
## [1] "άνγκελα_μέρκελ"

# query for specific line
dbGetQuery(con, "select * from test_table where col_one = 'άνγκελα_μέρκελ'")$col_one
## character(0)


# BUT this works half way through
dbExecute(con, "insert into test_table (col_one) values ('άνγκελα_μέρκελ')")
## [1] 1

dbGetQuery(con, "select * from test_table")$col_one
## [1] "άνγκελα_μέρκελ" "άνγκeλa_µέρκeλ" 

dbGetQuery(con, "select * from test_table where col_one = 'άνγκελα_μέρκελ'")$col_one
``` 

title: extension median ignores LIMIT
description:
It appears that the "median" extension to RSQLite ignores line selectors such as ORDER BY and LIMIT.

For example - using the attached database...

```
# install.packages("RSQLite")
library(DBI)

SQLiteIsHere <- "ucs_satellite.db" 
mySQLiteDB <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(),SQLiteIsHere)

RSQLite::initExtension(mySQLiteDB)

randomMedianSQL <- function() {
  do_this_sqlite <- "
    SELECT median(`Launch Mass (kg.)`)
    FROM satellites
    WHERE `Launch Mass (kg.)` != ''
    ORDER BY RANDOM()
    LIMIT 100
  "
  
  median(dbGetQuery(mySQLiteDB,do_this_sqlite))
}

randomMedianSQL() # returns 700
```

700 is the median of ALL values in the database.
i.e.
`median(UCS_Satellite_Database$Launch.Mass..kg.., na.rm = TRUE)`
returns 700.

It appears that median is ignoring the last two lines:
```
    ORDER BY RANDOM()
    LIMIT 100
```

My thanks for your work on this!

[ucs_satellite.db.zip](https://github.com/r-dbi/RSQLite/files/2330269/ucs_satellite.db.zip)

title: Connecting to a locked database, message that looks like an error
description:
Prints this: 
```
Error in rsqlite_send_query(conn@ptr, statement) : database is locked
```
which is very misleading, because it does create the valid connection, and this is not really an error, just a message. I am not sure where it is coming from, maybe from the C client and then it is hard to fix. To reproduce, just create a DB from one process (or the shell), and lock it, then connect from another process:

```
❯ sqlite3 /tmp/xxx
SQLite version 3.8.5 2014-08-15 22:37:57
Enter ".help" for usage hints.
sqlite> BEGIN EXCLUSIVE;
```

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "/tmp/xxx")
#> Error in rsqlite_send_query(conn@ptr, statement) : database is locked
con

#>  Path: /private/tmp/xxx
#>  Extensions: TRUE
```

title: Allow named supersets
description:
If you have a big named list or dataframe and you want to interpolate a few of its items into a parametrized statement, it would be nice to be able to say

     dbGetQuery(db,
         "select * from T where
             part = :partnumber and place = :city",
         mylist)

But as is, this code produces the error `Named parameters not used in query`. `db_bind` has a parameter `allow_named_superset`, but there's no way to pass `allow_named_superset = TRUE` because `dbBind` forces `allow_named_superset = FALSE`.

title: Multicore SQLite
description:
Hi

I get the following error message when I try to write to a SQLite DB file on a cluster computing machine: Couldn't set synchronous mode: database is locked

I know the cause that is several cores try to write to the same DB at or nearly the same time. Then the locking mechanism leads to the error. I am wondering whether the Serialized option can solve this issue? See https://www.sqlite.org/threadsafe.html
